cat >| /home/nick/work/andesim/Containerfile <<'DOCKER'
# AndeSim image -- one build produces everything a run needs.
#
# Build it with scripts/build_image.sh, which is the supported interface:
#
#   scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <riscv-toolchain-root>
#
# What this build does, and why it is shaped this way:
#
#   * It obtains and builds QEMU and the cycle-accurate engine itself. Users
#     do not prepare either one; that setup burden is what the image removes.
#   * It builds exactly ONE engine, named by ENGINE. Verilating the RTL is by
#     far the slowest step, and v0.1.0's image supports only this engine.
#   * The engine's RTL comes from the private Andes RD-SW repositories, so the
#     clone steps need a credential. It arrives as a build SECRET, reaching
#     only the RUN steps that clone -- never a layer, never build history.
#   * The RISC-V toolchain is NOT copied in. It is bind-mounted read-only at
#     /opt/riscv-toolchain (scripts/build_image.sh passes --volume), both here
#     and at run time, so the image carries no host path.

ARG VERILATOR_IMAGE=docker.io/verilator/verilator:v5.046
ARG BASE_IMAGE=docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04

FROM ${VERILATOR_IMAGE} AS verilator

# --- env: one build environment for QEMU, the engine, and AndeSim itself -----
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE} AS env

ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends \
      autoconf autoconf-archive automake autotools-dev bison ca-certificates \
      clang cmake curl flex g++ git help2man libboost-date-time-dev libboost-dev \
      libboost-filesystem-dev libboost-system-dev libfl-dev libfl2 \
      libglib2.0-dev libpixman-1-dev libreadline-dev libtool lld m4 make \
      ninja-build patch perl perl-doc pkg-config python3-dev python3-pybind11 \
      python3-venv python3-yaml ccache tclsh xz-utils zlib1g zlib1g-dev \
    && apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY --from=verilator /usr/local/share/verilator /usr/local/share/verilator
COPY --from=verilator /usr/local/bin /usr/local/bin

# Read the private repositories without leaving the credential behind: the
# secret is only readable inside the RUN steps that mount it.
ENV GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 \
    GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
    GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
    GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=/run/secrets/gitcreds"

# --- qemu: the functional leg, built here so the user never builds it --------
FROM env AS qemu-build

ARG QEMU_REPO
ARG SRC_REF
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch "${SRC_REF}" "${QEMU_REPO}" /src/qemu

# AndeSim is 64-bit-only, so riscv64-softmmu is the whole target list.
# --enable-plugins is what the hybrid handoff plugin needs.
RUN cd /src/qemu \
 && ./configure --prefix=/opt/qemu --target-list=riscv64-softmmu \
      --enable-plugins --disable-werror --disable-libnfs \
 && make -j"$(nproc)" \
 && make install \
 && rm -rf /src/qemu

# --- engine: the cycle-accurate leg, exactly one config ----------------------
FROM env AS engine-build

ARG VSIM_REPO
ARG SRC_REF
ARG ENGINE

# Only the submodules this engine needs: the shared libraries, plus the one RTL
# package its config names. Cloning every RTL package would multiply the build
# for engines this image does not ship.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch "${SRC_REF}" "${VSIM_REPO}" /src/vsim \
 && cd /src/vsim \
 && RTL=$(python3 -c "import yaml,sys; c=yaml.safe_load(open('config.yaml'))['cpus']; \
print(c['${ENGINE}']['rtl_package'])") \
 && echo "engine ${ENGINE} needs RTL package: ${RTL}" \
 && git submodule update --init --recursive -- \
      external/andes_clarity external/andesim_abi \
      external/cpu_config_to_march_converter external/doctest external/fmt \
      external/lief external/rapidjson external/spdlog external/systemc \
      external/systemc-cci external/systemc-components external/toml11 \
      external/yaml-cpp "external/${RTL}"

RUN cd /src/vsim \
 && cmake -B build -G Ninja \
      -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/andescycle \
      -DVSIM_LINK_STATIC=ON \
      -DVSIM_CPUS="${ENGINE}" \
 && cmake --build build --target "sim_${ENGINE}" \
 && cmake --install build \
 && strip "/opt/andescycle/bin/sim_${ENGINE}" \
 && rm -rf /src/vsim

# --- andesim: the driver, the handoff plugin and the runtime library ---------
FROM env AS andesim

ARG ENGINE
ENV QEMU_BIN_DIR=/opt/qemu/bin \
    VSIM_BIN_DIR=/opt/andescycle/bin \
    HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain \
    VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu/bin/qemu-system-riscv64 \
    VSIM_PLUGIN=/opt/andesim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so

COPY --from=qemu-build   /opt/qemu       /opt/qemu
COPY --from=engine-build /opt/andescycle /opt/andescycle
COPY . /opt/andesim
WORKDIR /opt/andesim

# The image's own config.env. Every consumer that reads it -- the driver, the
# build scripts, the test harness -- then resolves in-image paths, with no
# trace of the machine the image was built on.
RUN printf '%s\n' \
      "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}" \
      "QEMU_BIN_DIR=${QEMU_BIN_DIR}" \
      "VSIM_BIN_DIR=${VSIM_BIN_DIR}" \
      > config.env

# build_runtime.sh compiles against the mounted toolchain; only AndeSim's own
# artifacts (libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs) are baked.
RUN make -C qemu_plugin \
 && ./scripts/build_driver.sh \
 && ./scripts/build_runtime.sh \
 && ./build/andesim engines | grep -qw "${ENGINE}"

ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/andesim/andesim"]
DOCKER
cat >| /home/nick/work/andesim/.containerignore <<'IGN'
# The build context is the repo's sources only: git history and host build
# artifacts must never reach the image (they would bake this machine's state,
# and stale host binaries would shadow the ones the image builds).
.git
.gitmodules
build/
config.env
.pytest_cache/
**/__pycache__/
*.log
IGN

run     run one simulation (the default: 'run' may be omitted)
  fast      QEMU only -- functional, full speed

    --pc-start <sym|0x>       REQUIRED for --trigger pc  ROI start boundary

  --engine <id>               pick an engine, e.g. vsim:ax45mpv_premium (default: the sole one)

  --dry-run                   print the exact engine command(s) and exit, running nothing (fast/cycle/hybrid)

  --verify                    cross-check the hybrid run against a QEMU oracle

  --log-level <0-6>           verbosity, vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off (default 2: program output + the cycle figure)
  --log-file <file>           append EVERY level's messages (timestamped) to <file>; the console keeps --log-level
  --step-timeout-ms <ms>      hybrid per-leg spawn timeout (default 90000); raise it for a large ROI on the cycle-accurate leg

cat >| /home/nick/work/andesim/scripts/run_in_container.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run andesim inside the AndeSim image (see Containerfile, built by
# scripts/build_image.sh) -- the macOS path: macOS is run-only, because both
# hybrid legs must share one Linux kernel.
#
# Three rules make a containerised run behave like a local one:
#   1. The shared mmap stays VM-local: the container's /dev/shm (--shm-size)
#      is tier 1, and the host's HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never forwarded -- a host
#      path would be a virtiofs mount, where MAP_SHARED is not coherent.
#   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
#      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
#      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
#   3. The RISC-V toolchain is bind-mounted read-only at the canonical
#      in-image path. The image deliberately does not carry a toolchain; it
#      is the user's, and the image's own config.env already names this path.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# The canonical in-image toolchain mount point, shared with the image build.
IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain

ENGINE="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
if [ -z "$ENGINE" ]; then
  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=podman
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=docker
  else
    echo "andesim: a macOS run executes inside a Linux VM and needs podman (or docker)" >&2
    echo "           install podman and run: podman machine init && podman machine start" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
fi

# VERSION is the single source of truth for the tag scripts/build_image.sh
# applies, so a version bump cannot desync the build from the run.
IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION" 2>/dev/null || echo latest)}"
SHM_SIZE="${ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE:-3g}"   # tier 1 ceiling inside the VM
ENTRY="${ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY:-/opt/andesim/andesim}"

# The toolchain the caller has: the exported value, else config.env's.
TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
if [ -z "$TOOLCHAIN" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  TOOLCHAIN=$(sed -n 's/^HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=//p' "$ROOT/config.env" | tr -d '"' | head -1)
fi
TOOLCHAIN_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$TOOLCHAIN" ] && [ -d "$TOOLCHAIN" ]; then
  TOOLCHAIN_ARGS=(-v "$TOOLCHAIN:$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN:ro")
fi

TTY_ARGS=()
if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then TTY_ARGS=(-it); fi

exec "$ENGINE" run --rm "${TTY_ARGS[@]}" \
  --shm-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  -v "$PWD:$PWD" \
  "${TOOLCHAIN_ARGS[@]}" \
  -w "$PWD" \
  "$IMAGE" "$ENTRY" "$@"
SH

p='tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_macos_container.sh'
s=open(p).read()

  || fail "default runtime image name absent:"$'\\n'"$ARGV"''',
'''printf '%s\\n' "$ARGV" | grep -qx "andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION")" \\
  || fail "default image name (andesim:<VERSION>) absent:"$'\\n'"$ARGV"''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY

git checkout -b issue-24-image-build 2>&1 && git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1
feat(image): one build produces a runnable AndeSim image (behavioral)

Closes the setup burden the container was supposed to remove. The old
Dockerfile.runtime built only the driver and expected the user to have
already built QEMU and an engine themselves, then mount both in at run
time -- which is exactly the hard part.

scripts/build_image.sh is now the one command:

  scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <riscv-toolchain-root>

Behind it, Containerfile obtains and builds QEMU (riscv64-softmmu,
plugins enabled) and exactly one cycle-accurate engine
(ax46mpv_fpga_l3, via vsim's -DVSIM_CPUS), then builds the handoff
plugin, the driver and the runtime library. Only the RTL package that
engine's config names is cloned; Verilating RTL is the slowest step, so
building more engines than v0.1.0 ships would multiply the build.

The toolchain is NOT copied into the image. It is bind-mounted
read-only at /opt/riscv-toolchain, both during the build (so the
runtime library compiles) and at run time, so the image carries no
host path. The image writes its own config.env naming in-image paths.

The credential for the private RD-SW repositories arrives as a build
secret, so it reaches only the RUN steps that clone and never lands in
a layer or in build history. Access is checked before the build starts
rather than hours in, and the failure says access is required.

run_in_container.sh now reaches for that image: tag and entry point are
derived from VERSION, the single source of truth shared with the build,
and the toolchain is mounted when the caller has one.

Refs #24.

content.text: 現在補上最關鍵的缺口 —— 對「已建好的 image」本身做驗證（沒有 image 時乾淨跳過）：

input.command:
cat >| /home/nick/work/andesim/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_image_contents.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Issue #24 contract, verified against a built image: what the image actually
# contains. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_image_build.sh covers the build
# plan; this covers the product of that plan.
#
# Skips when the image has not been built on this machine -- building it takes
# hours (Verilating the RTL), so it cannot be a precondition of the standard
# suite. Build it with scripts/build_image.sh, then this runs for real.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

ENGINE=ax46mpv_fpga_l3
IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain
IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION")}"

RUNTIME="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
if [ -z "$RUNTIME" ]; then
  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then RUNTIME=podman
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then RUNTIME=docker
  else ok "no container runtime here -- skipping image contents"; exit 0
  fi
fi

if ! "$RUNTIME" image exists "$IMAGE" 2>/dev/null; then
  ok "$IMAGE not built here -- skipping image contents (scripts/build_image.sh)"
  exit 0
fi

# in_image CMD...  -- run a shell command inside the image, nothing mounted.
in_image() {
  "$RUNTIME" run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "$IMAGE" -c "$1" 2>&1
}

# --- the image runs AndeSim with no QEMU and no engine prepared outside ------
out=$(in_image '/opt/andesim/andesim list engines')
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qw "$ENGINE" \
  || fail "the image does not report the $ENGINE engine:"$'\n'"$out"

# Exactly one cycle-accurate engine. Every other config is deferred, and each
# one would add a Verilator run to the slowest step of the build.
engines=$(in_image 'ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR" | grep "^sim_" | sort')
[ "$engines" = "sim_$ENGINE" ] \
  || fail "the image must hold sim_$ENGINE and nothing else, found:"$'\n'"$engines"

out=$(in_image '"$VSIM_QEMU" --version')
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'qemu' \
  || fail "the image's QEMU does not run:"$'\n'"$out"

# The handoff plugin and the runtime library are AndeSim's own artifacts; the
# runtime library existing proves the mounted toolchain built it.
in_image 'test -f "$VSIM_PLUGIN"' \
  || fail "the hybrid handoff plugin is missing from the image"
in_image 'test -f /opt/andesim/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a' \
  || fail "the runtime library is missing -- the build-time toolchain mount failed"

# --- the toolchain is the user's, mounted; the image carries neither it nor -
# --- any path from the machine that built the image -------------------------
left=$(in_image "ls -A $IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN 2>/dev/null | wc -l")
[ "$left" = "0" ] \
  || fail "$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN holds $left entries -- a toolchain was baked in"

cfg=$(in_image 'cat /opt/andesim/config.env')
printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Eq "^HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN\$" \
  || fail "the image's config.env does not name the mount point:"$'\n'"$cfg"
printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Eq '/local/|/home/' \
  && fail "the image's config.env carries a host path:"$'\n'"$cfg"

in_image 'test -e /opt/andesim/.git' \
  && fail "the image carries the repository's git history"

ok "image contents: driver + QEMU + exactly the $ENGINE engine, no baked toolchain"
SH
chmod +x /home/nick/work/andesim/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_image_contents.sh

content.content:
# --- qemu: the functional leg, built here so the user never builds it --------
FROM env AS qemu-build

ARG QEMU_REPO
ARG QEMU_REF
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    install -m600 /run/secrets/gitcreds /tmp/gitcreds \
 && GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
    GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
    GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=/tmp/gitcreds" \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch "${QEMU_REF}" "${QEMU_REPO}" /src/qemu; \
    rc=$?; rm -f /tmp/gitcreds; exit $rc

# AndeSim is 64-bit-only, so riscv64-softmmu is the whole target list.
# --enable-plugins is what the hybrid handoff plugin needs.
RUN cd /src/qemu \
 && ./configure --prefix=/opt/qemu --target-list=riscv64-softmmu \
      --enable-plugins --disable-werror --disable-libnfs \
 && make -j"$(nproc)" \
 && make install \
 && rm -rf /src/qemu

# --- engine: the cycle-accurate leg, exactly one config ----------------------
FROM env AS engine-build

ARG VSIM_REPO
ARG VSIM_REF
ARG ENGINE

# Only the submodules this engine needs: the shared libraries, plus the one RTL
# package its config names. Cloning every RTL package would multiply the build
# for engines this image does not ship.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    install -m600 /run/secrets/gitcreds /tmp/gitcreds \
 && export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
 && export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
 && export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=/tmp/gitcreds" \
 && git clone --depth 1 --branch "${VSIM_REF}" "${VSIM_REPO}" /src/vsim \
 && cd /src/vsim \
 && RTL=$(python3 -c "import yaml,sys; c=yaml.safe_load(open('config.yaml'))['cpus']; \
print(c['${ENGINE}']['rtl_package'])") \
 && echo "engine ${ENGINE} needs RTL package: ${RTL}" \
 && git submodule update --init --recursive -- \
      external/andes_clarity external/andesim_abi \
      external/cpu_config_to_march_converter external/doctest external/fmt \
      external/lief external/rapidjson external/spdlog external/systemc \
      external/systemc-cci external/systemc-components external/toml11 \
      external/yaml-cpp "external/${RTL}"; \
    rc=$?; rm -f /tmp/gitcreds; exit $rc

RUN cd /src/vsim \
 && cmake -B build -G Ninja \

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -2
fix(image): per-repo source refs, and a credential store that can write (behavioral)

The first real build failed twice in the clone step.

The two source repositories do not share a branch name: the engine's is
llamacpp, QEMU's is andesim. One SRC_REF for both asked git for a
branch that does not exist. Each repository now carries its own ref,
overridable with --qemu-ref / --vsim-ref.

The pre-flight did not catch it, because `git ls-remote` exits 0 with
empty output when the ref is absent -- it only proved the repository was
readable. It now judges the ref by what came back and names the missing
one before the build starts, which is the whole point of a pre-flight
in front of a build this long.

Inside the build, git's `store` credential helper WRITES back to its
file on success, so pointing it at the read-only secret mount failed
with "unable to write credential store". Each clone step now takes a
writable copy of the secret and deletes it in the same layer, so no
credential is committed to the image. That wiring is per-step instead
of a stage ENV, which also stops it surviving into the image a user
receives.

Refs #24.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

input.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/30b29460-d3b2-45ab-8c40-064cecb652d5/scratchpad && cat >| /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/30b29460-d3b2-45ab-8c40-064cecb652d5/scratchpad/issue-24-update.md <<'MD'
## Decisions taken, replacing the UNRESOLVED section

**How the build authenticates to the private repositories: a build-time secret.**

Of the three approaches this ticket listed, the first is implemented:
`scripts/build_image.sh` passes the credential with `podman build --secret`,
and only the two `RUN` steps that clone mount it. It never becomes a layer and
never appears in the finished image's build history, which is what ruled out
passing it as an ordinary build argument. Requiring the user to clone the
repositories on the host beforehand stays rejected -- it re-imposes the setup
burden this ticket exists to remove.

Two details the mechanism forced:

- git's `store` credential helper writes back to its file on success, so it
  cannot point at the read-only secret mount. Each clone step takes a writable
  copy and deletes it in the same layer.
- The two repositories do not share a branch name: the engine's source is on
  `llamacpp`, QEMU's on `andesim`. The refs are per-repository, overridable
  with `--qemu-ref` / `--vsim-ref`.

## Amendment: the toolchain is mounted, not baked

This ticket required the toolchain to "end up inside the image". It does not.
It is bind-mounted read-only at one canonical in-image path,
`/opt/riscv-toolchain`, both while the image is built (so AndeSim's own runtime
library gets compiled against it) and when a container runs.

Reasons this is the better shape:

- The image carries no path from the machine that built it. The image writes
  its own `config.env` naming `/opt/riscv-toolchain`, so every consumer that
  reads it -- the driver, the build scripts, the harness -- resolves in-image
  paths. That also stops this ticket from working against the "no author
  machine state" requirement tracked separately.
- The toolchain is the user's, is large, and is licensed separately. Baking a
  copy of it into every image buys nothing.

The user still names it exactly once, at build time:

```sh
scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <riscv-toolchain-root>
```

The consequence for the acceptance scenarios: "I mounted nothing into the
container beyond my own working directory" becomes "beyond my own working
directory and my toolchain". Nothing else changes -- no QEMU and no engine has
to be prepared or mounted, which was the point.
MD

content.text:
QEMU 那一段已經完整通過了（用 secret clone → configure → 2702 個 object → 安裝到 `/opt/qemu/bin`），RTL package 解析也對（`ax46mpv_fpga_l3 → ax46mpv_advanced`）。

但引擎那一段撞到一個**不在 andesim repo 的 blocker**：

`hybrid_vsim@llamacpp` 把 `external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` 釘在 `f62337b`，**這個 commit 只存在你這台機器上**（遠端 master 是 `ba7adda`）。所以任何乾淨 clone（包括客戶的）都 build 不起來 —— 這是 repo 完整性問題，不是我的 Containerfile 問題。

那個沒推的 commit 加的是 qemu.cfg 產生器的 `smstateen`，只在 `NDS_RVH_SUPPORT` 或 `NDS_SMSTATEEN` 為真時才作用。`ax46mpv_fpga_l3` 是 `NDS_RVH_SUPPORT=0` 且沒有 SMSTATEEN，**所以對 v0.1.0 這顆引擎，遠端 master 產生的 qemu.cfg 完全一樣**。

這需要推到別的 repo，得你決定：

content.text:
**它是什麼**

`cpu_config_to_march_converter` 是 **hybrid_vsim 的一個 git submodule**，不是 andesim 的東西：

| | |
|---|---|
| 在 hybrid_vsim 裡的路徑 | `external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` |
| 遠端 | `gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter` |
| 你本機 | `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` |

**它做什麼**

裡面有 `scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py`。vsim 的 `cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake:151` 在 build 每顆引擎時跑它一次：把 RTL 的 `config.inc`（那堆 `NDS_*` define）翻譯成 QEMU 的 `-readconfig` cfg，烤在 `config.inc` 旁邊。之後 `sim_<cpu> --print-qemu-config` 把它吐出來，andesim driver 用它讓 **QEMU（fast leg）的 ISA 跟 cycle 引擎一致**。

沒有它的話，`VerilatorHelpers.cmake:162` 會塞一個空 cfg，driver 就退回預設 `-cpu` —— 那正是你記憶裡那類 fast leg 太寬鬆、cycle leg 才抓到違規的 bug 來源。所以不能關掉它。

**問題在哪**

```
hybrid_vsim@llamacpp  →  釘 external/cpu_config_to_march_converter = f62337b
遠端 RD-SW/...        →  master = ba7adda   （沒有 f62337b）
```

fix(run): let the image's own ENTRYPOINT receive the user's arguments (behavioral)

A containerised run died with "andesim run --mode hybrid: unexpected
argument 'run'". The wrapper passed the in-image driver path as the
first argument on top of the image's ENTRYPOINT, so the driver saw its
own path as an operand.

The bug predates the image work -- Dockerfile.runtime declared the same
kind of ENTRYPOINT and the wrapper passed the path just the same. It
survived because the contract test drives a stub container engine that
only records argv, so nothing ever ran. The test even pinned the wrong
shape: it asserted the entry path was present. It now asserts what
matters, that the argument after the image name is the user's own
first argument, and a real containerised hybrid run reports 56 cycles
through this path.

ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY stays available, applied as --entrypoint, which is
the only way that works.

Refs #24.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG

input.command:
SP=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/30b29460-d3b2-45ab-8c40-064cecb652d5/scratchpad; python3 - <<'PY'
p='/tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/30b29460-d3b2-45ab-8c40-064cecb652d5/scratchpad/issue-24-update.md'
s=open(p).read()
s += '''
## Amendment: the build clones all three sources; the context is empty

The image build takes nothing from the machine it runs on. It clones AndeSim,
QEMU and the engine itself, and the build context is an empty directory whose
emptiness is enforced rather than assumed.

That closes a hole the first working version still had: with the working tree
as the build context, the image's AndeSim half came from whatever state the
building machine happened to be in -- a stale `build/` directory, a local
`config.env`, an uncommitted edit -- which is the same class of problem the
image exists to remove. The finished image now reports what it was built from:

```
AndeSim   v0.1.0 (issue-24-image-build/7454b8d)
  abi     main/9ecc0cc
  qemu    10.2.3
  engine  ac4937c
```

The accepted cost: a local change must be pushed before an image can carry it.
`--andesim-ref` names the branch.

The git history is dropped once the driver is built -- its version stamp is
baked at compile time, so the image needs no repository metadata.

## Bugs the real build found

Every one of these only shows up in a clean environment, which is the argument
for gating a release on an actual image build (#23):

1. The source repositories do not share a branch name -- the engine's is
   `llamacpp`, QEMU's is `andesim`. One ref for both asked git for a branch
   that does not exist.
2. The pre-flight did not catch that, because `git ls-remote` exits 0 with
   empty output when a ref is absent. It now judges the ref by what came back.
3. git's `store` credential helper writes back to its file on success, so it
   cannot point at a read-only secret mount.
4. QEMU's configure needs `bzip2`: riscv64-softmmu is one of the targets that
   ship edk2 blobs.
5. Both QEMU plugins are POSIX code compiled with `-std=c11`, which defines
   `__STRICT_ANSI__` and hides `PATH_MAX`, `write`, `fsync`, `ssize_t` behind
   glibc's `__USE_POSIX` guards. It built on the Arch workstation, whose libc
   headers leak them, and failed on Ubuntu 24.04.
6. The run wrapper passed the in-image driver path as an argument on top of the
   image's ENTRYPOINT, so the driver saw its own path as an operand. This one
   predates the image work: `Dockerfile.runtime` declared the same kind of
   ENTRYPOINT, and the contract test drove a stub engine that only recorded
   argv, so nothing ever ran.

A separate finding, in `hybrid_vsim` rather than here: its `llamacpp` branch
pinned `external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` at a commit that existed only
on one workstation, so no clean clone anywhere could build the engine. Fixed
upstream by re-pinning to a pushed commit.

## Verified

Built from an empty directory, with only a toolchain path named:

- the image holds the driver, QEMU 10.2.3, and `sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3` and no
  other engine
- `/opt/riscv-toolchain` is empty in the image; the toolchain is mounted
- the image's `config.env` names in-image paths only, with no host path
- fast mode runs: `hello from QEMU1`
- hybrid mode runs and reports a cycle count: `[andesim] 56 cycles`
- a fixture compiles inside the image against the mounted toolchain
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git push -q origin issue-24-image-build && git log --oneline -1
fix(image): pin each source by commit, so a moved branch is not silently reused (behavioral)

A rebuild after pushing new commits produced a byte-identical image:
podman reported "Using cache" for the clone step and the finished image
still said it was built from the previous commit. A clone layer's cache
key is its instruction text, and a branch name never changes, so the
build silently shipped stale sources -- which defeats the point of
cloning the sources in the first place, and would hand a release gate
the wrong tree.

scripts/build_image.sh now resolves each ref to a commit on the host
and passes it as a build argument, so the cache key moves when the
branch does. Each clone then asserts it landed on that exact commit,
which also closes the window between resolving and cloning.

The resolution replaces the separate pre-flight: it does both jobs, and
it now runs for --dry-run too, so the plan a dry run prints is the plan
a real build runs.

The contract test drives three local repositories instead of the real
remotes, so it pins this behaviour with no network and no credentials.

Refs #24.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG

input.command:
M=/home/nick/.claude/projects/-home-nick-work-andesim/memory; cat >| $M/vsim-submodule-pins-must-be-pushed.md <<'MD'
---
name: vsim-submodule-pins-must-be-pushed
description: hybrid_vsim submodule pins that exist only on a workstation break every clean clone; the andesim image build and any release gate cannot build the engine.
metadata:
  type: project
---

The andesim image build clones `hybrid_vsim` from the remote and runs
`git submodule update --init --recursive`, so **every submodule commit
`hybrid_vsim` pins must be reachable on that submodule's own remote.**
A pin that exists only in a local checkout fails as:

```
fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref <sha>
```

Hit for real on 2026-09-08: `llamacpp` pinned
`external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` at a commit never pushed to
`RD-SW/cpu_config_to_march_converter`. No clean clone anywhere -- not the image
build, not a customer -- could build the engine. Fixed by re-pinning to the
remote's `master`.

Checking a pin: `git ls-remote` is NOT the test. It lists only ref tips, so a
pin on a ref's ancestor looks missing when it is fine. Use a real fetch:

```sh
git init -q /tmp/probe && git -C /tmp/probe fetch -q --depth 1 <url> <sha>
```

Relevant to the release gate ([[gitea-issue-tracker]] issue 23, "a real image
build"): the gate catches this class only because it clones from the remote.
The same applies to `hybrid_qemu` and `hybrid_sim`. Note the three repos do not
share a branch name -- engine `llamacpp`, QEMU `andesim`.

推了新 commit 後重建，podman 對 clone 那步回報 `Using cache`，產出的 image **依然報舊 commit**。因為 layer 的 cache key 是指令文字，分支名永遠不變 —— build 會靜靜地拿舊程式碼。這會讓 release gate (#23) 拿到錯的樹。

修法：`build_image.sh` 在 host 端把三個 ref 各自解析成 commit 當 build arg 傳進去，cache key 就會隨分支移動；每個 clone 再斷言自己確實落在那個 commit（順帶關掉「解析到 clone 之間 tip 又動」的空窗）。同時這個解析取代了原本的 pre-flight（一件事做兩用），而且 `--dry-run` 也走同一條路徑，所以 dry-run 印的計畫就是真實計畫。

- image 裡有 driver、QEMU 10.2.3、`sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3`，**沒有**其他引擎
- `/opt/riscv-toolchain` 在 image 裡是空的；config.env 只有容器內路徑，沒有你機器的路徑
- fast mode：`hello from QEMU1`
- hybrid mode：`[andesim] 56 cycles`（直接跑 + 走 wrapper 兩條路徑都是）
- fixture 在容器內用掛載的 toolchain 編譯成功

The path is not empty — **it does not exist at all.** The Containerfile never creates the mountpoint; the build-time `--volume` mount is transient and leaves nothing behind. No toolchain ships, which is the point, but see fragility #2.

This host has a real Docker 29.5.1 at `/usr/bin/docker`, and `docker build --help` has **no `--volume` option** (BuildKit dropped it). The constructed command is podman-only. Harmless here (podman is preferred and present), but the documented interface is wrong.

2. **The toolchain is in no layer's cache key, yet a cached layer is built against it.** Containerfile STEP 12 runs `build_runtime.sh`, which compiles `libandesim_runtime.a`/`crt0.o` with the bind-mounted toolchain. That mount contributes nothing to the cache key. Rebuild with a *different* toolchain and the same three revs, and podman reuses the runtime artifacts compiled against the *old* toolchain — silently. This is exactly the stale-source failure the Containerfile header says it designed away for refs, left open for the toolchain.

3. **Forgetting the mount gives a raw error, not a diagnostic.** With no `-v`, a fixture build ends in `make: /opt/riscv-toolchain/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc: No such file or directory / Error 127`. Because the directory doesn't exist (#c above), there's nothing in the image to hint at what to mount. `config.env` and `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` both point at a dangling path.

4. **Minor:** the empty build context is a fixed path (`/tmp/andesim-empty-context`) and the script dies if anything is in it. Any stray file there breaks all future builds with a message that reads like an attack warning.

5. **Minor:** `ENTRYPOINT` is `/opt/andesim/andesim` (a 773-byte bash wrapper), but STEP 12 only verifies `./build/andesim list engines`. The wrapper's existence is never asserted. It is present and works.

Clean on the security claims I could check: the host credential string appears nowhere in `podman history`, no `/home/nick` or `/local/nick` path appears in history, `/tmp/gitcreds` and `/root/.git-credentials` are absent, and `/opt/andesim/.git` was removed. Fast mode also runs fine with no toolchain mounted, since the ELF is prebuilt — the mount is only needed for compiling.</result>

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# build_image.sh -- the one command that builds a runnable AndeSim image.
3	#
4	#   scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <path> [--tag NAME] [--dry-run]
5	#
6	# The user names a RISC-V toolchain once, here. Everything AndeSim itself
7	# builds -- AndeSim itself, QEMU, the ax46mpv_fpga_l3 cycle-accurate engine,
8	# the handoff plugin, the driver and the runtime library -- is cloned and built
9	# by the image build, so a run needs nothing prepared beforehand.
10	#
11	# All three sources are cloned by the build, and the build context is empty.
12	# Nothing from the host reaches the image: it cannot inherit a stale build/
13	# directory, a local config.env or an uncommitted edit, and it is reproducible
14	# from the three refs alone. The flip side is that a local change must be
15	# pushed before an image can carry it.
16	#
17	# The toolchain is never copied into the image. It is bind-mounted read-only at
18	# one canonical in-image path (IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN below), both while the image is
19	# built and when a container runs, so the image carries no host path.
20	#
21	# Building requires read access to the Andes RD-SW repositories on
22	# gitea.andestech.com: the engine's RTL comes from them. Access is checked
23	# before the long build starts, not hours into it.
24	set -uo pipefail
25	
26	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
27	
28	# The engine v0.1.0's image ships. Exactly one is built: Verilating the RTL is
29	# the slowest step of the whole build.
30	ENGINE=ax46mpv_fpga_l3
31	IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain
32	
33	# The three source repositories, each with its own ref: they do not share a
34	# branch name, and assuming two of them did cost a build. Overridable so an
35	# image can be built from a different line of development.
36	ANDESIM_REPO="${ANDESIM_ANDESIM_REPO:-https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git}"
37	QEMU_REPO="${ANDESIM_QEMU_REPO:-https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_qemu.git}"
38	VSIM_REPO="${ANDESIM_VSIM_REPO:-https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_vsim.git}"
39	ANDESIM_REF="${ANDESIM_ANDESIM_REF:-llamacpp}"
40	QEMU_REF="${ANDESIM_QEMU_REF:-andesim}"
41	VSIM_REF="${ANDESIM_VSIM_REF:-llamacpp}"
42	
43	usage() {
44	  cat >&2 <<'USAGE'
45	usage: scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <path> [--tag NAME] [--dry-run]
46	
47	  --toolchain <path>  RISC-V toolchain root on this machine (must contain
48	                      bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc). Bind-mounted read-only,
49	                      never copied into the image.
50	  --tag NAME          image tag (default: andesim:<VERSION>)
51	  --andesim-ref REF   branch/tag of the AndeSim source (default: llamacpp)
52	  --qemu-ref REF      branch/tag of the QEMU source (default: andesim)
53	  --vsim-ref REF      branch/tag of the engine source (default: llamacpp)
54	  --dry-run           print the build plan and exit
55	USAGE
56	}
57	
58	die() { echo "build_image.sh: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
59	
60	TOOLCHAIN=""
61	TAG=""
62	DRY_RUN=0
63	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
64	  case "$1" in
65	    --toolchain) TOOLCHAIN="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
66	    --tag)       TAG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
67	    --andesim-ref) ANDESIM_REF="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
68	    --qemu-ref)  QEMU_REF="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
69	    --vsim-ref)  VSIM_REF="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
70	    --dry-run)   DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
71	    -h|--help)   usage; exit 0 ;;
72	    *)           usage; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
73	  esac
74	done
75	
76	[ -n "$TOOLCHAIN" ] || { usage; die "--toolchain is required"; }
77	[ -x "$TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" ] \
78	  || die "$TOOLCHAIN has no bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -- name a RISC-V toolchain root"
79	TOOLCHAIN="$(cd "$TOOLCHAIN" && pwd)"
80	
81	# The toolchain's identity, by content. The layer that compiles AndeSim's
82	# runtime library uses the bind-mounted toolchain, and a bind mount
83	# contributes nothing to a cache key -- so without this, rebuilding with a
84	# different toolchain silently reuses artifacts compiled against the old one.
85	# Hashed, so the host path never reaches the image's build history, and by
86	# content rather than path so merely moving a toolchain does not force a
87	# rebuild. It tracks the compiler, not every library under the root: a
88	# hand-edited newlib beside an unchanged gcc is not distinguished.
89	TOOLCHAIN_ID=$( { "$TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" --version 2>/dev/null | head -1
90	                  sha256sum "$TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" | cut -d" " -f1
91	                } | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
92	[ -n "$TAG" ] || TAG="andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION" 2>/dev/null || echo latest)"
93	
94	ENGINE_CMD="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
95	if [ -z "$ENGINE_CMD" ]; then
96	  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE_CMD=podman
97	  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE_CMD=docker
98	  else die "need podman (or docker) on PATH to build the image"
99	  fi
100	fi

103	# build secret, so it reaches only the RUN steps that clone and never lands in
104	# a layer or in the image's build history.

106	
107	# --- resolve each ref to a commit -------------------------------------------
108	# Two jobs at once. It fails now, with a reason, rather than hours into the
109	# build when a ref is missing or the repositories are unreadable. And it pins
110	# the sources by commit, which the clone layers need: their cache key is the
111	# instruction text, so a branch name alone never changes and a build against a
112	# branch that has moved would silently reuse the old clone and ship stale
113	# sources. A --dry-run resolves too, so the plan it prints is the real plan.
114	[ -r "$CREDENTIALS" ] \
115	  || die "no git credentials at $CREDENTIALS -- building the image requires read" \
116	         "access to the Andes RD-SW repositories on gitea.andestech.com"
117	
118	# ls-remote exits 0 with no output when the ref is absent, so the ref is
119	# judged by what came back, not by the exit status.
120	resolve_ref() {
121	  local repo="$1" ref="$2" line
122	  line=$(GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 \
123	         GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
124	         GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
125	         GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=$CREDENTIALS" \
126	         git ls-remote --heads --tags "$repo" "$ref" 2>/dev/null | head -1) \
127	    || die "cannot read $repo -- building the image requires access to the Andes" \
128	           "RD-SW repositories on gitea.andestech.com (the engine's RTL comes from them)"
